claim: A visa office in Gulshan, Dhaka, took seven people to India and Nepal on 12 March 2024 for 'visa processing' for Europe; they were sent back from India on 28 June 2024
The victims later found the Gulshan office padlocked
BDT 80 lakh was taken from those seven people
A man promised the United States was flown to Nepal on 7 December 2023 and locked in a godown in Kathmandu, where his phone, passport and papers were taken
He was forced to send his father a voice message saying he had reached Mexico, after which the family paid the balance
The family paid BDT 45 lakh in all
In arbitration the accused signed a stamp paper promising to repay BDT 45 lakh plus BDT 1 lakh compensation, and according to the victim paid nothing
A Jashore man promised a labour job in Australia was taken to Kathmandu, Nepal, on 14 September 2025 and held in a hotel, where his passport and dollars were taken and more money demanded
Before he left he was given papers presented as an Australian visa grant and sent for a medical test and fingerprinting in Uttara, Dhaka
The family paid a BDT 1,500,000 fee and BDT 150,000 more as ransom; he was still missing in April 2026
A Madaripur man was promised a work permit for Morocco and onward travel to Spain or Italy for BDT 17 lakh
At the airport in Egypt the group's passports were taken for 23 hours and returned with Libyan visas
He was told the Libyan visa was only for transit to Morocco
He came home after 104 days, after ransom was paid
Two women were told their route to Italy was legal and that the Italian embassy paperwork would be completed in Egypt
In Egypt their passports and phones were taken and they were locked in a room; they were held about a year and a half
The ring told people they would reach Italy through Serbia and Belarus, but sent them first to countries in Asia and the Middle East and then through Nepal or Sri Lanka to Egypt or Libya
It took BDT 2,000,000 to 2,500,000 per person, and up to BDT 4,000,000 in some cases
Its firms were named 'Arzu Immigration Limited' and 'Nafis Air Immigration Limited'
A Noakhali man who contracted to reach Italy for BDT 1,200,000 was sent through New Delhi, Colombo, Sharjah and Cairo before being driven into Libya
He was kept about 16 days in Colombo while his family was asked for more money, and held about five days in a house in Cairo until USD 6,000 was paid
He had handed his passport to an office in Ashkona, Dhaka
Men promised jobs in Cuba were taken through Kolkata, Delhi, Singapore and Fiji to Vanuatu and locked in an isolated house
Vanuatu police rescued 103 more Bangladeshis
On 12 November 2024 the Barishal Human Trafficking Tribunal sentenced two brothers to life imprisonment in the case
A group of ten promised jobs in Cyprus was taken to Saudi Arabia on Hajj visas, kept there several weeks, then flown to Russia and bused to an army camp
Passengers given tickets for Nepal and Italy and passports carrying fake Italian Schengen visas flew on 26 May 2026, were held two days at Rome airport and sent back on 28 May
They had agreed to pay BDT 3,000,000 each and paid BDT 2,000,000 each in advance
CID arrested a Biman Bangladesh Airlines ground-service junior officer in the case
The usual route to Italy runs from Bangladesh to Nepal, India or Sri Lanka, then Dubai, then Egypt or Tunisia, then Libya, then across the Mediterranean
